To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mTORC2 kinase activity and downstream Akt signaling are positively regulated by merlin, and that mTORC1 signaling is negatively regulated by merlin.
merlin positively controls the mTORC2 kinase, and mTORC2 activity is attenuated upon acute merlin loss in cells.
merlin positively affects mTORC2 activity in cells and that this effect is not consistently maintained in NF2-defective tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of neurofibromatous disorders and developing new therapeutic strategies for treating these diseases.
identifying the molecular pathways that are dysregulated in neurofibromin 2-deficient tumors. In particular,
the identification of novel mechanisms of merlin function in the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NF2 gene product, Merlin, is a negative regulator of mTOrC1 signaling and a positive regulator of mTORC 2.
the mTOR signaling pathways in NF2-associated schwannoma and meningioma are different from those observed in TSC.
mTORC2 is a novel and direct merlin target in cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
merlin is a negative regulator of mTOrC1 signaling in meningioma and Schwann cells, but a positive regulator of mTORC 2 signaling.
we identified mTORC2 as a novel target for merlin and that mTORC2 may be a suitable target for NF2-related tumors.
NF2-deficient tumors, such as meningiomas and Schwann cells, exhibit hyperactive mTOR complex  signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mTORC2 plays a critical role in the regulation of Akt signaling in normal arachnoids and Schwann cells and that this function may be impaired in NF2-associated tumors, but to a lesser extent.
mTORC2 plays an important role in regulating the growth and survival of normal and merlin-deficient cells.
the two mTOR complexes are differentially regulated by merlin, and that mTORC2 is a novel merlin-regulated kinase.
